thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: multi-GPU inference cluster reporting NCCL communicator errors and occasional container crashes on tp4-prod-*-pods. Severity: P1. Paging oncall aisha and eng-sre.

aisha: I'm on it. seeing alerts for increased 502s to /v1/generate in us-east-1 and GPU nodes in tp4 pool showing repeated NCCL WARN logs. tagging miguel.

miguel: grabbing logs now. early glance: repeated lines like `NCCL WARN Call to recv/comm timed out` then containers OOM or crash with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` and `XID 79` on a subset of ranks. could be memory corruption or driver + kernel mismatch.

aisha: customer-impact? CS?

customer-success-jay: acme-analytics seeing degraded tail-latency and 502s for the streaming endpoint. They've flagged multiple live jobs failing mid-epoch. Customer on a dedicated SLA, notified already.

miguel: stack from pod tp4-infer-23:

```
2026-03-15T02:10:42Z NCCL INFO rank 1 : communicator created
2026-03-15T02:12:05Z NCCL WARN Call to recv timed out (rank 2 <-> rank 3) at nccl_comm.c:482
2026-03-15T02:12:06Z cudaCheck FAIL: 77 (cudaErrorIllegalAddress) in /workspace/runtime/comm_impl.c:314
2026-03-15T02:12:06Z terminating with signal 6 (ABRT)
```

miguel: kernel: 5.15.0-1023, nvidia-driver 525.85, cudnn 8.4. container shows recurrent OOMs before illegal address on rank that has pipeline-parallel apex blocks.

aisha: quick mitigation proposals:
- isolate/cordon nodes with repeated XIDs
- drain affected pods and restart on fresh hosts
- route traffic to fallback single-GPU model variant for acme-analytics (lower perf but stable)
- increase NCCL timeout/retry policy temporarily

tara: I'm taking next shift. I can perform cordon+drain once we agree. advise minimal config change to reduce blast radius.

aisha: agree. first do soft mitigation: update routing to point acme-analytics to model-redwood-v1-fallback in us-east-1 and enable circuit-breaker for streaming calls. miguel, can you push that now? @deploy-bot can we create a traffic shift rollout?

deploy-bot: Rollout request accepted: route acme-analytics -> model-redwood-v1-fallback (10m canary -> 100%). Executing.

miguel: routing change applied. telemetry shows acme error rate dropping from 18% -> 3% within 90s. leaving canary for 10m.

aisha: cordon nodes with >3 XID events. list: tp4-node-12, tp4-node-19, tp4-node-34. tara can drain-evict after checkpointing in-flight KV cache.

tara: starting drain on node-12. command:
```
kubectl cordon tp4-node-12
kubectl drain tp4-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```

miguel: note: before drain I'm going to capture /var/log/nvidia and dmesg from node-19 and tgz it to s3: s3://redwood-incident-archives/2540012345/node-19-logs.tgz

sre-bot: Captured GPU metrics: ECC errors spike on GPU0 of node-19, power draw ~320W, fan ramping. No thermal throttling. Kernel oops not observed.

aisha: good. after draining 12 and 19, restart the affected runtimes. miguel, can you bump NCCL timeout env var temporarily for the runtime to 5s -> 15s? path: /deploy/rt-configs/pp-infer.yaml

miguel: I can patch a ConfigMap with NCCL_RETRY_TIMEOUT=15000ms and do a rolling restart of the runtime pods in the tp4 pool, but that risks prolonged stalls. prefer restarting affected processes first.

aisha: do both: restart the crashed containers so they come up clean, then roll the config. we want to reduce immediate impact and avoid recurrent hangs.

tara: node-12 drained, pods rescheduled to other nodes. node-19 logs uploaded to s3. starting restart of runtime containers on rescheduled pods.

miguel: restarted runtimes on 6 affected pods. one pod failed to come up with same `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`. moving that workload to spare node tp4-node-58 and scaling down TP size for that job (TP rank -> reduce pipeline stages by 1).

aisha: scaling down TP size for the hot job is a good short-term workaround. it breaks strict affinity but preserves progress. take note for postmortem.

customer-success-jay: acme confirms improved behavior on fallback variant, but asks for ETA to full restore.

aisha: ETA: after cordon+drain of flagged nodes and rolling restarts + config change, estimate 30-45m for full restore and verification. will update in 15m.

miguel: applied ConfigMap patch: `NCCL_RECV_TIMEOUT_MS=15000` and triggered rolling restart. watching for increased SLO errors.

sre-bot: Observability: 502 rate back to baseline across most jobs. A small subset still reports transient errors correlated with a single remaining problematic GPU on tp4-node-34.

aisha: node-34 next to be isolated. tara, can you take the remainder and start a host-level driver rebind as a last resort? i.e., unload/reload nvidia modules and restart kubelet on the node.

tara: preparing maintenance window on node-34. informing oncall. command run:
```
sudo systemctl stop kubelet
sudo rmmod nvidia_drm nvidia_modeset nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia_modeset nvidia_drm
sudo systemctl start kubelet
```

tara: did the rebind, then reschedule pods. no repeated XIDs after the rebind for 12 minutes. one pod had an orphaned KV cache; I cleared the cache and warmed prefix cache from stored snapshots.

miguel: confirming: no new `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` in last 1200s across the pool. NCCL WARN spikes reduced. rolling restart completed.

aisha: good. rollback plan if recurrence: immediate traffic cutover to fallback cluster in another region (us-west-2), escalate to infra-driver team for driver patch or node replacement, and open support ticket with NVIDIA for XID 79 trace.

customer-success-jay: telling acme: we expect full restore and will run a follow-up with detailed timeline + RCA. they want a memo and timeline by EOD.

aisha: assigning postmortem owner: miguel. timeline: record events, root cause hypothesis (driver/firmware + memory-corruption triggering illegal address during cross-rank GPU comms), and remediation (node replacement policy, add ECC monitoring alerts, add runtime guardrails to reduce TP size on error). include follow-ups for Dedicated customers: fallback routing automation.

miguel: acknowledged. will capture logs: /var/log/nvidia, dmesg, runtime core dumps, NCCL trace logs, and job-level golden prompt traces for failing spans. posting artifact links shortly.

sre-bot: Incident marked: mitigated. P1 -> degraded (monitoring). Please add notes and assign postmortem when stable.

aisha: handing over to tara for night watch. tara, you'll be primary until 08:00 UTC. ping if anything flares.

tara: on it. will monitor GPU XID counts, NCCL warn rate, and client 5xxs dashboard. setting an alert for >3 XID events on a single node in 10m.

aisha: thanks everyone. final note: do not redeploy runtime binary without QA on a small canary — we might trigger the same edge-case hang.

customer-success-jay: acme acknowledged, asked for a post-incident summary and contact for escalation. I gave them miguel's alias.

miguel: uploaded artifact bundle: s3://redwood-incident-archives/2540012345/artifacts.tgz

sre-bot: Incident closed to oncall rotation. add postmortem link when ready.

tara: adding a short runbook blurb in the ops wiki: "TP NCCL hang triage: cordon -> drain -> rebind drivers -> fallback routing -> scale down TP size". will push after break.

aisha: thanks team. follow-ups: miguel postmortem, infra to replace nodes 19/34 if GPU HW anomalies persist, runtime to add guardrail for runtime memory sanitizer. :thumbsup:
